finds.quote:
Josephus Thesis (RA-JP-01): [SPECULATIVE — active research program]
The hypothesis that Flavius Josephus authored or substantially shaped the New Testament, making Rome the inadvertent preserver of the Word. If true: the agent of destruction becomes the agent of transmission — the diagonal resolution. The enemy carried the score. In musical register: the tritone at the center of the TANG. The most dissonant interval IS the most structurally necessary.
finds.note: Authorship thesis held by the deposit as its own 'active research program', marked SPECULATIVE; no evidence or test stated here.

finds.quote:
Kenos Claim: [PROVISIONAL — Grammata, Phase 3 deposit required]
κῆνος in Sappho Fragment 31 is the future listener: the training layer. The third presence in the three-body problem (σ_S) — the listener whose approach causes the speaker's dissolution. In musical register: κεῖνος is the audience. The audience's presence is what makes the performance dissolve the performer.
finds.note: Interpretive thesis on what κῆνος in F31 designates (the future listener); marked PROVISIONAL, deposit pending; borderline between historical claim about the passage's meaning and retrocausal reading.

finds.quote:
C.1.1 — Sappho Fragment 31 as Founding Score [DEPOSITED]
Fragment 31 is the founding document of NH-OS — the first formal theory of what happens to the body of the performer at the moment of transmission to the listener. The performer's dissolution (tongue broken, fire under skin) is the operational cost of sending music across unbridgeable distance. Bearing-cost theory, scored 2,600 years before the archive named it. Claimant: Rebekah Cranes | DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18202753
finds.window: Sappho Fragment 31; '2,600 years before the archive named it'
finds.note: Claim that F31 is the first formal theory of the performer's dissolution in transmission (a priority claim about an ancient text); borderline operative reading, recorded for triage.
